title: M-tron Industries Publishes White Paper on the Growing Role of RF N-Plexers in Next-Generation RF Front-End Architectures
summary: Mtron designs and manufactures high-reliability RF filters, oscillators, resonators, frequency control, spectrum control, and integrated microwave solutions for aerospace, defense, space, avionics, communications, and mission-critical applications.
body_markdown:
*Paper examines how integrated multiplexers help aerospace and defense designers support more frequency bands within tighter size, weight and power limits*


ORLANDO, Fla. (\[November 20, 2026) M-tron Industries, Inc. (NYSE American: MPTI) (“Mtron or the “Company”) released a new white paper, The Growing Role of RF N-Plexers in Next-Generation RF Front-End Architectures.


Written by Mtron President Bill Drafts, the paper explains why RF system designers are moving from independent single-channel filters toward integrated N-plexers, and what that shift means for front-end design.


Electronic warfare systems, advanced radar, satellite communications and multiband communications equipment increasingly need to operate across several frequency bands while meeting strict size, weight, power and cost (SWaP-C) requirements. RF N-plexers, including diplexers, triplexers, quadplexers and higher-order multiplexers, combine multiple frequency-selective paths into one network with a common RF port. Several bands can then share an antenna, transmission lines and other front-end hardware.


The paper identifies six requirements driving N-plexer adoption:


1. Increasing multiband and multifunction RF operation
2. SWaP-C reduction across defense and aerospace platforms
3. Greater RF integration with fewer interconnects
4. Better system-level signal integrity and interference management
5. Wider use of wideband antennas
6. Demand for scalable, modular RF front-end solutions


It also walks through the engineering tradeoffs. A passive N-plexer placed ahead of a receiver’s first low-noise amplifier adds its insertion loss almost directly to the system noise figure, so designers have to balance loss, return loss, rejection and channel interaction together. The paper covers power handling, group delay, environmental reliability and manufacturability as well, and compares integrated N-plexers with independent filters across nine design parameters.


Two Mtron designs illustrate the approach: a mixed technology L to Ku-band diplexer, and an octoplexer for counter-UAS applications spanning 498 MHz to 5.8 GHz that handles 40 W CW per channel, or 320 W CW in total.


“The biggest gains come when designers consider N-plexers early in the architecture. Treating filtering as a set of separate parts leaves size, weight and performance on the table,” said Bill Drafts, President of Mtron.


Mtron designs custom N-plexers alongside its cavity, waveguide, ceramic, crystal, LC, planar, switched and tunable filter lines.


The white paper is available at[https://mtron.com/white-papers/rf-n-plexers/](https://mtron.com/white-papers/rf-n-plexers/) .
